messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — throughput profile & quick clarifying Qs

Hi Samir — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size a Dakota-hosted pilot and draft an SLA sketch: 

1) Observed patterns you mentioned: several short searches (avg 12 tokens) from the store portal and longer product description generation (~250 tokens) from the catalog enrichment job. Can you confirm rough split: ~65% short, ~30% long, ~5% misc?

2) Peak characteristics: you said the marketing campaign produces ~2-minute peaks, roughly 10x baseline, but I want to confirm the sustained peak window — is the 10x over 2 minutes or sustained across a 10–15 minute rolling window?

3) Streaming: for the store assistant we need partial tokens delivered as soon as possible. Target tail p99 latency for first token is 250ms. Does that match your expectations?

Action I took: attached a one-page token profile template (nimbus_token_profile.csv) — fill columns A–D if you can (avg tokens, 95th, 99th, percent of requests). Also attached our quick SLO checklist for reference (slo_checklist.pdf).

Next steps: if you can return the token profile today or tomorrow we’ll run a quick cost + throughput sketch and propose a pilot capacity (dedicated pool estimate) by Friday. 

Thanks —
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 415-555-0132

From: Samir Agarwal <samir@nimbusretail.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Khanna <priyaa.k@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — throughput profile & quick clarifying Qs

Mateo — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Priya and I filled the CSV with the initial numbers (attached as a version in Drive). Quick answers inline: 

1) Split: yes — current estimates are 68% short (search/autocomplete), 28% long (catalog enrichment/batches), 4% other (admin tools).

2) Peak window: the marketing bursts typically last 3–4 minutes at full intensity; the tail can be 10–12 minutes at 2–3x baseline. So short spikes of 8–10x for ~3 minutes, then a decaying tail.

3) Streaming: store assistant first-token target of 250ms is aggressive but doable — we'd be comfortable with p95 < 200ms and p99 < 400ms for first token.

Additional: our concurrency behavior — store assistant opens ~120 concurrent sessions during peak, each session sending short prompts at irregular intervals. For catalog enrichment, jobs are batched overnight: 50 parallel tasks producing long outputs, but latency is not critical there.

Attaching: we provided a Drive link with the CSV and an export of a sample request trace (trace_20270427.json) if you want the raw.

Samir
VP Engineering, Nimbus Retail

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus pilot sketch & next steps (attachments included)

Samir / Priya — following up with a concise plan based on the numbers you provided. Summary bullets below plus attachments (nimbus_token_profile.csv updated with our parsed percentiles; slo_checklist.pdf with proposed targets and escalation windows).

Summary of our pilot assumptions (for review):
- Baseline qps (short requests): 60 QPS average, 68% of traffic => ~41 QPS short requests.
- Long requests (catalog outputs): 18 QPS average, 28% of traffic with avg 250 tokens each => ~4500 tokens/sec from that stream.
- Peak: 8–10x short request spikes for 3 minutes => transient peak short QPS up to ~330–410 QPS.
- Concurrency: estimate 120 active store sessions during peak; sustained per-session inter-arrival varies.
- Streaming: target first-token p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms. We'll enable partial-response streaming and tight tail-slo routing.
- Caching: with the 68% short mix we estimate a 55–70% prefix/KV cache hit rate; this reduces effective token compute during peaks.

Requested confirmations from Nimbus:
1) Confirm the 120 concurrent sessions estimate for peak is not per-region aggregated (we assume single US region).
2) Confirm catalog enrichment batch concurrency (50 parallel) is mostly offline; we will schedule these to low-cost windows during pilot.

Ops plan & next steps (timeline):
- Thu 29 Apr 5pm PST: Redwood ops (Sean) will validate the simulation and provide GPU slot estimate and 95/99 queueing numbers.
- Fri 30 Apr EOD: Redwood to send a one-page pilot capacity + cost estimate and an SLA sketch.
- Next Tue 4 May: kickoff call (30 mins) to walk pilot runbook and monitoring dashboard.

Attachments: nimbus_token_profile.csv (parsed), slo_checklist.pdf

If you see anything off in the assumptions above, flag it and I’ll update the sketch.

Best —
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
